result.title: Progressive Reliable Supervision for Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation
result.summary: Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation (B$^2$-UniDA) aims to adapt a target model to an unlabeled target domain under arbitrary label-space relationships, while neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible during adaptation. Under such restrictive information access, reliable target supervision is unavailable, while predictions from the black-box source model can be unreliable due to source bias and domain shifts. To address this challenge, we propose Progressive Reliable Supervision (PReS), which progressively establishes and refines reliable target supervision by coordinating complementary knowledge from the black-box source model, foundation models, and the evolving target model. PReS first identifies reliable known samples by exploiting semantic consistency under diffusion-based perturbations and cross-model consensus between the black-box source model and CLIP. It then estimates the sample-wise reliability of the two predictors and adaptively integrates their complementary predictions to construct reliable pseudo labels. The resulting supervision is exploited asymmetrically to encourage confident and discriminative predictions for reliable known samples while maintaining uncertain yet locally consistent predictions for potential unknown samples. As adaptation proceeds, the emerging target-domain knowledge is further leveraged to refine both the pseudo labels and the known/unknown sample partition, forming a closed-loop process in which supervision construction and target adaptation mutually reinforce each other. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets under diverse label-space relationships demonstrate that PReS achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance under the restrictive B$^2$-UniDA setting.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PReS，用于源数据与源模型参数均不可访问的黑盒通用域适应：借助扩散扰动下的语义一致性、黑盒源模型与 CLIP 的跨模型共识筛出可靠已知样本，再按样本级预测可靠度融合两路预测构造伪标签，并以闭环方式迭代精化伪标签与已知/未知划分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其样本级可靠度估计、跨模型一致性筛选与不对称监督构造，可能为 LVR 训练中的视觉证据筛选和监督贡献分配提供可核查线索，但该工作不涉及 latent 推理状态生成，迁移价值需进一步判断。
